tEn: OpenAI's Unreleased Model Astra Solves Ten Major Open Mathematics Problems
tZh: OpenAI 未发布模型 Astra 解决十大数学开放问题
sEn: OpenAI's unreleased model Astra solves ten major open mathematics problems.
sZh: OpenAI 未发布的模型 Astra 解决了十个重大数学开放问题。
absEn: This article discusses OpenAI's unreleased AI model, Astra, which reportedly solved ten major open mathematics problems in a single day, a feat that has significant implications for the field of mathematics and AI development. The core argument is that while the results are impressive, they also highlight a shift in expectations, as AI demonstrates superhuman capabilities in advanced math, similar to previous breakthroughs in cyber and coding. The author notes that other models, like Fable and Sol, can also solve some of these problems when pointed at them, but Astra's 'Juice'—its ability to independently identify and solve such problems—marks a potential step change. The article also explores the broader consequences, including the challenge of digesting AI-generated proofs, the risk of misalignment, and the acceleration of AI R&D timelines. The conclusion emphasizes that while this is a major milestone, it is not necessarily AGI, but it does move the goalposts and underscores the urgent need for careful management of AI's rapid advancement.
absZh: 本文讨论了 OpenAI 未发布的 AI 模型 Astra，据报道该模型在一天内解决了十大数学开放难题，这一成就对数学领域和 AI 发展具有重大意义。核心论点是，尽管结果令人印象深刻，但它们也突显了预期的转变，因为 AI 在高级数学方面展现了超人类能力，类似于之前在网络和编码方面的突破。作者指出，其他模型如 Fable 和 Sol 在指向这些问题时也能解决其中一些，但 Astra 的“Juice”——即独立识别并解决此类问题的能力——标志着一个潜在的阶跃变化。文章还探讨了更广泛的后果，包括消化 AI 生成的证明的挑战、错位的风险以及 AI 研发时间线的加速。结论强调，虽然这是一个重要的里程碑，但它不一定意味着 AGI，但它确实移动了目标，并强调了谨慎管理 AI 快速发展的紧迫性。

contrib.en: Astra independently identified and solved ten major open math problems in one day, a potential step change.
contrib.zh: Astra 在一天内独立识别并解决了十个重大开放数学问题，可能是能力阶跃。

contrib.en: Astra's 'Juice'—autonomously finding problems—distinguishes it from models solving them only when pointed.
contrib.zh: Astra 的“Juice”——自主发现问题——使其区别于仅在提示下解题的模型。

contrib.en: Results show AI is now superhuman at advanced math, like cyber and coding, though not superintelligence.
contrib.zh: 结果表明 AI 在高等数学上已超人，类似网络安全与编程，但并非超级智能。

contrib.en: Verifiable domains like math and coding advance fastest; progress depends heavily on verifiability.
contrib.zh: 数学、编程等可验证领域进步最快；进展高度依赖可验证性。

contrib.en: The result accelerates AI R&D timelines and raises urgency for careful management of rapid advancement.
contrib.zh: 该结果加速 AI 研发时间线，并凸显审慎管理快速进展的紧迫性。

contrib.en: It moves AGI goalposts: prior metrics no longer 'count', highlighting jagged, uneven capability growth.
contrib.zh: 它移动了 AGI 门槛：旧指标不再“算数”，凸显能力增长的不均衡与锯齿状。

limits.en: No control group: Fable and Sol solved about half the problems when pointed, suggesting elicitation effort.
limits.zh: 缺少对照组：Fable 与 Sol 在提示下解出约半数问题，说明存在集中引导效应。

limits.en: AI proofs are opaque; models cannot identify which steps are hard, hindering human digestion.
limits.zh: AI 证明不透明；模型无法指出哪些步骤困难，妨碍人类理解与消化。

limits.en: Success is confined to well-defined, verifiable problems with surrounding theory, not general research taste.
limits.zh: 成功局限于定义清晰、可验证且有周边理论的问题，而非通用研究品味。

limits.en: Verification is often not easier than generation; unverifiable domains may lag by orders of magnitude.
limits.zh: 验证往往不比生成容易；不可验证领域可能落后数个数量级。

limits.en: Risk of misalignment and deskilling: no humans may digest proofs, and optimization pressures may cease to be human.
limits.zh: 存在失准与去技能化风险：可能无人消化证明，优化压力也可能不再由人类主导。

paras.en: Daniel Litt: It's a big deal.
paras.zh: Daniel Litt：这是一件大事。

paras.zh: Claude Fable 5：以菲尔兹奖的尺度衡量，其中任何一项……都足以支撑起一份获奖理由。

paras.en: 1a3orn: If you give Fable the raw list of OpenAI's solved problems and ask it "What process made this list?" the number one proposal is "a fictional scenario trying to concretely explain what superhuman AI math would look like." Huh.
paras.zh: 1a3orn：如果你把 OpenAI 已解决问题的原始清单交给 Fable，并问它“是什么过程生成了这份清单？”，排名第一的答案是“一个虚构场景，试图具体说明超人类 AI 数学会是什么样子。”哈。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball: I'm actually not surprised by reactions like this from models to the Astra breakthroughs. Models tend to underestimate their own capabilities, I assume because they are trained on lots of web text about what ChatGPT could and couldn't do in 2023/4.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball：对于模型针对 Astra 突破给出这样的反应，我其实并不意外。模型往往会低估自身能力，我猜是因为它们训练时接触了大量关于 ChatGPT 在 2023/4 年能做什么、不能做什么的网络文本。

paras.en: Other instances are less impressed. But we should all agree: It's a big deal.
paras.zh: 其他实例则没那么印象深刻。但我们都应该同意：这是一件大事。

paras.en: Certainly that is a fantastic result for $2,000, but you also have to price in some of the costs of developing Astra in the first place, as well as the cost of any failed attempts.
paras.zh: 当然，对 2,000 美元来说这是一个极好的结果，但你还必须把最初开发 Astra 的部分成本，以及任何失败尝试的成本都计入其中。

paras.en: Nate Silver: Another question I'd have about the AI math breakthroughs is how they compare to the results you would have gotten if you'd budgeted the same amount of resources on human mathematicians and created incentives for them to go super hard on proofs.
paras.zh: Nate Silver：关于 AI 数学突破，我还有一个问题：如果把同等数量的资源预算给人类数学家，并为他们创造激励、让他们在证明上全力以赴，那么与这些结果相比会如何？

paras.en: There aren’t all that many working mathematicians, and most of them are academics with teaching responsibilities. So it’s possible that the labs represent a fairly high share of the aggregate amount of capital directed toward mathematical proofs in recent years.
paras.zh: 在职数学家并不多，而且他们大多是承担教学职责的学者。因此，这些实验室在近年来投向数学证明的总资本中可能占有相当高的份额。

paras.en: My guess is that in the short term, if you budget more money to mathematicians to go harder, you don’t get that much of a force multiplier if they are not spending the money on compute. They’re still allowed to buy coffee to turn it into theorems, but that has rapidly diminishing returns.
paras.zh: 我的猜测是，短期内，如果你给数学家更多预算让他们更努力，而他们不把钱花在算力上，那么你不会得到太大的力量倍增效应。他们仍然可以买咖啡，把它转化为定理，但这样做的回报会迅速递减。

paras.en: The problem is that the mathematicians can hand off some classes and hire a little help, but they were already pretty motivated to work hard on proofs, and there are not that many good mathematicians, and training more of them takes many years, and the best mathematicians are a lot more talented and productive than the second tier. I am guessing the main thing you could do is lure a bunch of top level math talent to stay in or return to academia.
paras.zh: 问题在于，数学家可以移交一些课程并雇一点帮手，但他们本来就已经很有动力去努力做证明，而且优秀的数学家并不多，培养更多这样的人需要很多年，而最顶尖的数学家比第二梯队的数学家更有才华、更高效。我猜你能做的主要事情是吸引一批顶级数学人才留在或回到学术界。

paras.en: What you can do is point the mathematicians towards different problems. You still need to find places they have curiosity, but yes if you suspected these particular problems were solvable you could get more shots at these particular goals.
paras.zh: 你能做的是引导数学家去研究不同的问题。你仍然需要找到他们有好奇心的领域，但没错，如果你怀疑这些特定问题可解，你就能在这些特定目标上获得更多尝试机会。

paras.en: As I understand math, it would likely take years to see those results if those involved are shifting focus into new problem areas. Mathematicians usually need a while to struggle with and understand these kinds of problems before they can make progress.
paras.zh: 据我对数学的理解，如果相关人员将焦点转向新的问题领域，可能需要数年才能看到那些结果。数学家通常需要一段时间来挣扎和理解这类问题，然后才能取得进展。

paras.en: Indeed, Alexander Gerko points to a different problem. There are not even enough mathematicians to process all the 'vibe researched' math results as it is, let alone what we will get with Astra and then models after Astra. If we get, as he predicts, 50 years of math progress in 2 years, who is even going to understand the results? What counts as worthy of a new mathematics PhD when he says over the last month he got AI to do several PhDs worth of math results?
paras.zh: 事实上，Alexander Gerko 指出了另一个问题。目前甚至没有足够的数学家来处理所有“凭感觉研究”（vibe researched）出来的数学成果，更不用说我们将会从 Astra 以及 Astra 之后的模型那里得到的东西了。如果如他所预测的那样，我们在 2 年内取得 50 年的数学进展，那么还有谁能理解这些结果呢？当他说过去一个月里他让 AI 做出了相当于好几个博士论文水平的数学成果时，什么才算得上配得上一个新的数学博士学位呢？

paras.en: Fable reacted to this in at least one case by calling this 'the most important day in mathematics.' The consensus is that Fable was taking things way too far if you are judging purely by the results, as impressive as they are.
paras.zh: Fable 至少在一个场合对此做出反应，称这是“数学史上最重要的一天”。共识是，如果纯粹从结果来评判，尽管这些结果令人印象深刻，Fable 的说法还是太过头了。

paras.en: Jared Duker Lichtman: To be clear, the OpenAI result is far from the "most important day in the history of mathematics" or similarly hyperbolic statements.
paras.zh: Jared Duker Lichtman：需要明确的是，OpenAI 的成果远非“数学史上最重要的一天”或类似的夸张说法。

paras.en: However, it is concrete evidence that the rate of progress is steep, and we may not be so far away from such a day.
paras.zh: 然而，这确实是进展速度陡峭的具体证据，我们可能离这样的一天并不遥远。

paras.en: Taelin: that said, what *was* the most important day in the history of mathematics?
paras.zh: Taelin：话虽如此，那么*究竟*哪一天才是数学史上最重要的一天呢？

paras.en: Wogan: I’d go with Principia Mathematica. Proving that 1+1=2 from first principles is pretty notable, I think!
paras.zh: Wogan：我会选择《数学原理》。从第一性原理证明 1+1=2 是相当了不起的，我认为！

paras.en: The other reason the day is big is that this changes expectations. If we get these ten results now, what about more results soon?
paras.zh: 这一天之所以重要的另一个原因是，这改变了预期。如果我们现在得到了这十项结果，那么很快会有更多结果吗？

paras.en: So, yes, very impressive. It’s a big deal.
paras.zh: 所以，是的，非常令人印象深刻。这是一件大事。

paras.en: AI is now superhumanly capable at cyber and coding and superhuman at advanced math, the same way non-AI computers have been superhuman at basic math for a long time. This is distinct from superintelligence, which is a higher bar.
paras.zh: AI 现在在网络和编程方面具有超人类的能力，在高级数学方面也具有超人类的能力，就像非 AI 计算机长期以来在基础数学方面具有超人类能力一样。这与超级智能不同，超级智能是一个更高的标准。

paras.en: Often the move is to try and rationalize this as ‘oh okay sure it is superhuman at exactly the things it is superhuman at now, but not at other things, and also it is already superhuman so it cannot get substantially better than it already is.’
paras.zh: 通常的做法是试图将其合理化为‘哦，好吧，当然它在现在具有超人类能力的那些事情上是超人类的，但在其他事情上不是，而且它已经是超人类了，所以它不能比现在更好多少。’

paras.en: Nabeel S. Qureshi: Both math and cyber are existence proofs for superhuman intelligence now, so if you're still a skeptic you need a strong case for other knowledge work domains being somehow harder to crack than these. Or you could update all the way and come to terms with it all.
paras.zh: Nabeel S. Qureshi：数学和网络这两个领域如今都已成为超级智能的存在性证明，因此，如果你仍然持怀疑态度，就需要给出强有力的理由，说明其他知识工作领域为何会比这两个领域更难攻克。或者，你也可以彻底更新自己的认知，并接受这一切。

paras.en: A lot of people DMing me like "these results aren't REALLY that impressive, you're an idiot!" are unfortunately engaging in the very human impulse to cope. It makes sense, we've never faced this kind of thing before. But it's happening!
paras.zh: 很遗憾，许多私信我的人说“这些结果其实没那么令人印象深刻，你是个白痴！”，他们只是在顺应一种非常人性化的应对冲动。这可以理解，我们以前从未面对过这类事情。但它正在发生！

full.sec: Could We Have Called Sol or Fable?
full.secZh: 我们本可以叫它 Sol 或 Fable 吗？

paras.en: Yes, for at least some of these questions, if we already knew where to look.
paras.zh: 是的，至少对其中一些问题而言，前提是我们已经知道该往哪里找。

paras.en: Levent Alpoge, who had Fable disprove the Jacobian Conjecture, pointed Fable at these ten problems, and in a day had solved five of them.
paras.zh: Levent Alpoge 曾让 Fable 证伪了雅可比猜想（Jacobian Conjecture），他把这十个问题交给 Fable，一天之内就解决了其中五个。

paras.zh: Gary Marcus：🚨 突发、令人捧腹的消息：Astra 问题中有一半可以被 Fable 解决。OpenAI 甚至没有设置对照组。而你们大多数人还上当了！

paras.en: Elliot Glazer: This aligns with my suspicion that Astra isn't a step change beyond Sol. The 10-breakthrough drop was a concerted elicitation effort by OAI and partially Sol-achievable. IMO, o3 and Sol have been the step changes in autonomous mathematics; all else is the long arc of scaling.
paras.zh: Elliot Glazer：这与我的怀疑一致，即 Astra 并非超越 Sol 的阶跃式变化。那 10 项突破的下降是 OAI 一次协同的引导努力，且部分可由 Sol 实现。在我看来，o3 和 Sol 才是自主数学领域的阶跃式变化；其余都只是 Scaling（规模扩张）的长期弧线。

paras.en: Gary Marcus: "Astra isn't a step change beyond Sol."
paras.zh: Gary Marcus：“Astra 并非超越 Sol 的阶跃式变化。”

paras.en: All those who tried to gaslight me this weekend, all I can do is … laugh hysterically.
paras.zh: 所有这个周末试图对我进行煤气灯操纵的人，我能做的只有……歇斯底里地大笑。

paras.en: This is likely a repeat of what happened with Mythos and cyber.
paras.zh: 这很可能是 Mythos 和 cyber 事件的重演。

paras.en: Mythos has what I call ‘The Juice,’ the ability to find and string together exploits without anyone knowing what to be looking for.
paras.zh: Mythos 拥有我称之为‘The Juice’的能力，即能够在无人知晓该寻找什么的情况下，发现并串联起漏洞利用。

paras.en: Once you know what you are looking for, and point another model at the exact code snippet, usually Sol or Opus and often Kimi or GLM and so on can also find any particular vulnerability. They cannot string them together on their own at the same level, and they cannot go looking for anything at all in the same way. This crosses a threshold where in practice you would point Mythos at code and have it go looking for anything at all.
paras.zh: 一旦你知道要寻找什么，并将另一个模型指向确切的代码片段，通常 Sol 或 Opus，以及经常 Kimi 或 GLM 等也能找到任何特定的漏洞。它们无法以同等水平自行串联这些漏洞，也无法以同样的方式去寻找任何东西。这跨越了一个阈值，在实践中，你会将 Mythos 指向代码，让它去寻找任何东西。

paras.en: Astra has a similar version of The Juice with respect to this kind of defined advanced math. You can point it at a variety of major open problems, and it will crack some of them, and this fact motivated OpenAI to actually look for such advancements. Now that we’ve seen this, you can point Fable or Sol at these questions, and sometimes they solve them.
paras.zh: Astra 在定义明确的高级数学方面拥有类似版本的 The Juice。你可以将它指向各种重大开放问题，它会破解其中一些，这一事实促使 OpenAI 真正去寻找此类进展。既然我们已经看到了这一点，你可以将 Fable 或 Sol 指向这些问题，有时它们能解决。

paras.en: IA’s question is on point. You do this to calibrate advancements and capabilities in math, and because we are following curiosity. Levent is doing a cool public service.
paras.zh: IA 的问题很中肯。你这样做是为了校准数学领域的进展和能力，并且因为我们追随好奇心。Levent 在做一项很酷的公共服务。

paras.en: Other people are pointing Fable or Sol at various unsolved problems. They are sometimes getting good results, like the disproof of the Jacobian conjecture. That is worth doing, but success is rarer.
paras.zh: 其他人正将 Fable 或 Sol 指向各种未解决的问题。他们有时会得到不错的结果，比如对雅可比猜想的反证。这值得做，但成功较为罕见。

paras.en: That Fable and Sol can do these problems once asked does not change our answer to ‘how good at math is Astra?’ Rather it changes our answer of how good Fable and Sol are, which does inform the question of whether Astra is a step change a la Mythos. I don’t think we have enough information, from the outside, to answer that question yet.
paras.zh: Fable 和 Sol 在被要求后能够解决这些问题，并不改变我们对“Astra 的数学能力有多强？”的回答。相反，它改变了我们对 Fable 和 Sol 有多强的回答，而这确实有助于回答 Astra 是否像 Mythos 那样是一次阶跃变化的问题。我认为，从外部来看，我们还没有足够的信息来回答这个问题。

paras.en: I do think that it would have been more responsible of OpenAI to have had a control group, at least in terms of asking Sol, and giving it at least a similar budget. Of course I understand why they did not do that. It would be worse marketing, so why do more work to do worse marketing? Because science, because reputation, because all the good things. One would hope.
paras.zh: 我确实认为，OpenAI 如果设置一个对照组会更负责任，至少在对 Sol 的提问上，并给予它至少相似的预算。当然，我理解他们为什么没有这样做。那会是不那么好的营销，所以为什么要做更多工作来做更差的营销呢？因为科学，因为声誉，因为所有美好的事物。人们会希望如此。

paras.en: Still, I get it. OpenAI still did a super cool thing. They were still the first ones to actually Do The Thing and publish a result. That’s what counts. My name in Dnepropetrovsk is cursed, because OpenAI has published first.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，我理解。OpenAI 仍然做了一件超级酷的事情。他们仍然是第一个真正完成这件事并发表结果的人。这才是最重要的。我在第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克的名字被诅咒了，因为 OpenAI 先发表了。

paras.en: Meanwhile, yeah, sometimes it really is that one guy in Dnepropetrovsk named Dan.
paras.zh: 与此同时，是的，有时候真的就是第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克那个叫 Dan 的家伙。

paras.en: neppy: As an insider, my experience with AI for math is that when it's a problem not in my field I'm like, "holy shit math is so cooked", and when it's a problem in my field I'm like, "lmao an AI mogged Dan" (Dan is the only one who seriously tried the problem in the last decade).
paras.zh: neppy：作为一名内部人士，我对 AI 做数学的体验是：当问题不属于我的领域时，我会想“天哪，数学要完蛋了”；而当问题属于我的领域时，我会想“笑死，一个 AI 把 Dan 碾压了”（Dan 是过去十年里唯一认真尝试过这个问题的人）。

paras.en: davidad: Human researchers who have an appetite to take on truly hard problems and human researchers who are smart enough to fruitfully work on truly hard problems are not usually the same humans. This does give humans a somewhat unfair disadvantage.
paras.zh: davidad：有胃口去攻克真正难题的人类研究者，和聪明到足以在真正难题上做出成果的人类研究者，通常并不是同一批人。这确实给了人类某种不太公平的劣势。

paras.en: Also humans need to sleep. And also humans aren't already broadly familiar with all knowledge published before 2026 in every discipline. It's not very fair at all, really.
paras.zh: 而且人类需要睡觉。而且人类也并非已经广泛熟悉 2026 年之前每个学科发表的所有知识。说真的，这根本一点都不公平。

paras.en: Regardless of whether this extends to unverifiable domains, quite a lot of what constitutes AI R&D very much has verification available. If you speed something up, you know you sped it up. We have a lot of metrics one can maximize, not at the level of math but at a similar level to things like code and cyber.
paras.zh: 无论这一点是否延伸到不可验证的领域，构成 AI 研发的相当多内容其实都具备可验证性。如果你加速了某件事，你就知道它被加速了。我们有许多可以最大化的指标，其水平虽不及数学，但与代码和网络攻防等领域相近。

paras.en: That is the main reason this result matters. The math progress is cool. Over time I expect it to result in other cool things.
paras.zh: 这正是该结果之所以重要的主要原因。数学上的进展固然很酷。随着时间推移，我预期它会带来其他很酷的成果。

paras.en: Whoever gets traction on true AI R&D self-improvement loops is going to suddenly find themselves in an overwhelmingly strong position. Knowing where you are relative to the other players becomes crucially important when things start accelerating more, and more information sharing on this would allow everyone to feel less pressure to be reckless. It stops meaningfully being a 'race' once the takeoff fully starts, to the extent that was ever the right metaphor.
paras.zh: 任何在真正的 AI 研发自我改进闭环上取得进展的人，都会突然发现自己处于压倒性的强势地位。当事情开始加速得越来越快时，了解自己相对于其他参与者的位置就变得至关重要，而在这方面更多地共享信息，会让所有人感到不必那么铤而走险。一旦起飞真正开始，它就不再具有‘竞赛’的意义了——如果那曾经是个恰当比喻的话。

paras.en: Yo Shavit speculates that OpenAI might be in an increasingly strong position for AI R&D, due to its focus on RL, TTC and math proving translating well into AI R&D tasks. My guess is that this is not the case, and Anthropic's specializations matter at least as much and probably moreso. OpenAI has invested a lot in RL, but recent events have shown the need to kind of teardown and rebuild quite a lot of that, and have illustrated some of the reasons why the important investments in deep alignment will be so important in the next phase.
paras.zh: Yo Shavit 推测，OpenAI 可能在 AI 研发方面处于日益强势的地位，因为其对强化学习（RL）、TTC 和数学证明的专注能够很好地迁移到 AI 研发任务中。我的猜测是情况并非如此，Anthropic 的专长至少同样重要，甚至可能更重要。OpenAI 在强化学习上投入了大量资源，但近期事件表明，其中相当大一部分需要推倒重建，并且已经说明了为什么对深度对齐的重要投入在下一阶段会如此关键。

paras.en: One possible thing that happens if OpenAI proceeds too recklessly is that their AI is misaligned and all is lost and we get a Bad Ending and maybe all die. Another is that their AI is misaligned, and this becomes increasingly obvious and a barrier to using that AI to do the work that matters, and they have to keep pausing or reworking and they fall behind.
paras.zh: 如果 OpenAI 推进得过于鲁莽，可能发生的一种情况是：他们的 AI 未对齐，一切尽失，我们迎来一个坏结局，也许全都死掉。另一种情况是：他们的 AI 未对齐，而这一点变得越来越明显，成为用该 AI 去做重要工作的障碍，他们不得不不断暂停或返工，从而落后于人。

full.sec: They Still Don’t See What Is The It That Is Coming
full.secZh: 他们仍未看清即将到来之物究竟是什么

paras.en: For example, Daniel Litt can see a future where AIs prove math theorems and no humans digest the proofs, but he thinks this would be because of deskilling. He does not realize this will be because there are no humans around to do the digestion.
paras.zh: 例如，Daniel Litt 能预见到这样一个未来：AI 证明数学定理，而没有人去消化这些证明；但他认为这会是技能退化（deskilling）所致。他没有意识到，这将会是因为周围根本没有人类来做消化工作。

paras.en: Elliot Glazer: I think the incomprehensible marvels prediction is a naive extrapolation of e.g. computer-found mates in 500+ moves, which have ~irreducible complexity. Powerful math phenomena (and technological breakthroughs) will have human-digestible nuggets of arbitrary granularity.
paras.zh: Elliot Glazer：我认为“不可理解的奇迹”这一预测，是对诸如计算机在 500 步以上找到将杀这类现象的天真外推，而这些现象具有约不可约的复杂性。强大的数学现象（以及技术突破）会带有任意粒度、可供人类消化的内核。

paras.en: Daniel Litt: I agree with this but I think there's a plausible future (which I would like to avoid) where no humans digest them.
paras.zh: Daniel Litt：我同意这一点，但我认为存在一个看似合理的未来（我希望避免它），其中没有人类去消化它们。

paras.en: Alex Kontorovich: What purpose would there be for creating things in silico for which humans find no value? At the end of the day, someone is paying an electric bill. What does that *human* get out of producing random useless strings of 0s and 1s inside a computer?
paras.zh: Alex Kontorovich：在硅基（in silico）中创造人类认为毫无价值的东西，会有什么目的？归根结底，总得有人付电费。那个 *人类* 从在计算机内生成随机的、无用的 0 和 1 字符串中能得到什么？

paras.en: Daniel Litt: For me the nightmare scenario is: a moribund math academia playing the slot machine for theorems, failing to train the next generation, and then the subject dying as no one cares enough to continue. Not saying this is likely--I think we'll adapt--but it seems possible.
paras.zh: Daniel Litt：对我来说，噩梦般的场景是：死气沉沉的数学学术界像玩老虎机一样赌定理，未能培养下一代，然后这门学科因无人有足够兴趣继续而消亡。我不是说这很可能——我认为我们会适应——但它似乎是可能的。

paras.en: Carles Sáez: In that case probably pure math research will stop. Who is going to spend enormous sums of money to solve problems nobody can understand and nobody cares about?
paras.zh: Carles Sáez：那样的话，纯数学研究很可能会停止。谁会花巨额资金去解决没人能理解、也没人在意的问题呢？

paras.en: Daniel Litt: Yes, I agree.
paras.zh: Daniel Litt：是的，我同意。

paras.en: Max von Hippel: Alex why do you assume a human is paying the electric bill?
paras.zh: Max von Hippel：Alex，你为什么假设是人类在付电费呢？

paras.en: If the world goes well otherwise, I am not worried about people not studying math. The right kind of math person loves studying math. There will be plenty of time available for such pursuits, at all levels. I agree with Fernando Borretti on the other types of cope he lists at the link: The AI will have better taste and better everything else than you do, so no you won’t still be in the core math loop. But I think that a lot of math either exists outside of social contexts, or it exists in social contexts that can survive. Math competitions are a lot like chess and a lot of math work was famously useless. See the old joke about someone suggesting a mathematician’s work found an application and they say ‘you take that back.’
paras.zh: 如果世界在其他方面发展顺利，我并不担心人们不学习数学。真正适合学数学的人热爱研究数学。各个层次都会有充足的时间用于这类追求。我同意 Fernando Borretti 在链接中列出的其他几种应对方式：AI 会比你有更好的品味和更好的其他一切，所以你不会仍然处于数学的核心圈。但我认为很多数学要么存在于社会语境之外，要么存在于能够幸存的社会语境中。数学竞赛很像国际象棋，而且很多数学工作以无用而闻名。看看那个老笑话：有人暗示一位数学家的研究找到了应用，数学家说‘你收回这句话。’

paras.en: Similarly, I do not worry that humans, if they have control over resource allocation, will be unwilling to pay for work on advanced math in these future abundant worlds. Advanced math is cool and proves unexpectedly useful and we will have lots of surplus. We might ‘run out of math to do’ but we won’t leave the math undone.
paras.zh: 同样，我不担心人类，如果拥有资源分配的控制权，会不愿意为未来富足世界中的高等数学工作付费。高等数学很酷，并且被证明出人意料地有用，而且我们将会有大量盈余。我们可能会‘用完可做的数学’，但我们不会让数学被搁置不做。

paras.en: Whereas I very much do worry that once the AIs are out there doing superintelligent math things, they are soon also doing superintelligent everything else. And then soon the optimization pressures that dictate what happens are not human. We will not be the ones doing resource allocation. And, especially if this happens soon, likely we would not long survive afterwards.
paras.zh: 然而，我非常担心的是：一旦 AI 在外头做着超级智能的数学工作，它们很快也会把其他一切事情都做得超级智能。到那时，决定事态走向的优化压力很快就不再来自人类。进行资源分配的将不再是我们。而且，尤其是如果这一切很快发生，我们很可能在之后不久便难以存活。

paras.en: Why indeed would you assume a human is paying the electric bill? I barely even pay my own electric bill now.
paras.zh: 说到底，你凭什么假设付电费的是人类呢？我现在连自己的电费都几乎不付了。

paras.en: Nabeel S. Qureshi: Very true (from Scott Alexander): we have AIs that can play chess, prove theorems, create art, and write award-winning short stories, but few people feel that current AI counts as "AGI".
paras.zh: Nabeel S. Qureshi：非常正确（引自 Scott Alexander）：我们有人工智能可以下棋、证明定理、创作艺术、写出获奖短篇小说，但很少有人觉得当前的人工智能算得上“AGI”。

paras.en: For what it's worth, I do not think current AIs count as AGI yet. It's just funny that many of our prior metrics/predictions for AGI turn out not to "really count" in the ways we thought.
paras.zh: 无论如何，我认为当前的人工智能还算不上 AGI。只是有趣的是，我们之前许多关于 AGI 的指标/预测，结果并没有像我们想象的那样“真正算数”。

paras.en: Ruxandra Teslo: why do you think that is?
paras.zh: Ruxandra Teslo：你为什么这么认为？

paras.en: Nabeel S. Qureshi: Insufficiently general + low sample efficiency -- e.g. true AGI would not need tons of RL on expert financial models to get as good as the median investment banker, it could just invent them from first principles and do better in various ways. Same with many other examples.
paras.zh: Nabeel S. Qureshi：不够通用 + 样本效率低——例如，真正的 AGI 不需要在专家金融模型上进行大量强化学习才能达到普通投资银行家的水平，它可以直接从第一性原理出发发明这些模型，并在各方面做得更好。许多其他例子也是如此。

paras.en: Clearly you can get pretty damn far with whatever type of AI this is though, but I think for "real AGI" the "G" matters.
paras.zh: 显然，无论这种人工智能是什么类型，你都能走得相当远，但我认为对于“真正的 AGI”来说，“G”（通用）很重要。

paras.en: To what extent is that goalposts moving, versus realizing that we were wrong about what is intelligence and what would be strong evidence of AGI?
paras.zh: 在多大程度上是目标在移动，而不是我们意识到自己此前对什么是智能、什么才是 AGI 的有力证据判断有误？

paras.en: I see a mix of both. I can see the argument that the 'G' is about sample efficiency and performance out of distribution, and the frontier has been more jagged than we expected. I also increasingly respect the response that this is basically hogwash, 'AI is whatever hasn't been done yet' and it is becoming increasingly absurd to not admit we have what we were previously thinking about as AGI, the goalposts have moved a lot.
paras.zh: 我认为两者兼有。我能理解这样一种论点：其中的“G”（通用）关乎样本效率与分布外性能，而前沿进展比我们预想的更加参差不齐。我也越来越认同另一种回应：这基本上是胡说八道——“AI 就是尚未被做到的事”，而且越来越荒谬的是，我们不肯承认自己已经拥有了此前所设想的 AGI，目标已经移动了很多。

paras.en: I do not think Astra is AGI, as per the way we currently think about AGI, but I view the other position as totally valid.
paras.zh: 按照我们目前对 AGI 的理解，我不认为 Astra 是 AGI，但我认为另一种立场完全成立。

full.sec: The AI Solved His Favorite Problems
full.secZh: AI 解决了他最喜欢的问题

paras.en: This is the perspective of Henry Yuen, who spent a long time working on some of these problems, including finding results that Astra built upon. It hits hard.
paras.zh: 这是 Henry Yuen 的观点，他长期致力于其中一些问题，包括发现 Astra 所基于的结果。这让人深受触动。

paras.en: Henry Yuen: Some initial thoughts, and a complicated mix of feelings.
paras.zh: Henry Yuen：一些初步想法，以及复杂交织的感受。

paras.en: 1. Wow. I mean, Erdős problems are cool (I genuinely mean that), I didn’t know about the Jacobian conjecture before it got disproved. But this newest batch from OpenAI hits home in a way the previous announcements did not.
paras.zh: 1. 哇。我的意思是，Erdős 问题很酷（我真心这么认为），在 Jacobian 猜想被推翻之前我并不知道它。但 OpenAI 的这一最新成果比之前的公告更触动我心。

paras.en: New circuit lower bounds? A simple, easy-to-describe non-sofic group? Hardness of approximation for CVP without needing a unique games-like conjecture? I didn’t just hear about these problems from my friends or from seminars. I feel their importance in my bones; I deeply care about the answers to these questions.
paras.zh: 新的电路下界？一个简单、易于描述的非 sofic 群？无需类似唯一游戏猜想即可证明 CVP 的近似困难性？我不只是从朋友或研讨会上听说这些问题。我深切感受到它们的重要性；我深深关心这些问题的答案。

paras.en: 2. And then -- the kicker -- something that I personally spent a couple years on in grad school, leading to some of my proudest work: quantum parallel repetition theorems. I spent many hours, days, nights, weekends in cafes, in my office, at home, trying to understand Ran Raz’s classical parallel repetition theorem and whether I could prove a quantum version of it.
paras.zh: 2. 然后——关键的是——我 personally 在研究生院花了几年时间研究的东西，并带来了一些我最自豪的工作：量子并行重复定理。我花了无数小时、数天、数夜、周末在咖啡馆、办公室、家里，试图理解 Ran Raz 的经典并行重复定理，以及我是否能证明它的量子版本。

paras.en: This period of struggle was important for me. I learned a lot of mathematics from it, and most importantly I learned that I could solve hard problems that (some) people cared about. I wouldn’t want to trade that experience for anything.
paras.zh: 这段挣扎的时期对我很重要。我从中学习了很多数学，最重要的是，我学会了我可以解决（一些）人们关心的难题。我不愿意用任何东西来交换这段经历。

paras.en: 3. Now, to the math. In 2016 I proved a polynomial-decay theorem; the exponential-decay theorem was left open and has since remained one of my favorite problems. I always intended to come back to it. Actually, a month ago I tried to set GPT 5.5 on it, and it didn’t make very much progress.
paras.zh: 3. 现在，回到数学。2016 年，我证明了一个多项式衰减定理；指数衰减定理仍未解决，此后一直是我最喜欢的问题之一。我一直打算回到这个问题。实际上，一个月前我尝试让 GPT 5.5 来解决它，但它没有取得很大进展。

paras.en: A couple days ago Lijie Chen (@wjmzbmr1) sent me and a couple others a writeup. Life was busy so I didn’t get a chance to look, but I guess now the cat’s out of the bag so I probably should opine a bit.
paras.zh: 几天前，Lijie Chen（@wjmzbmr1）给我和其他几个人发了一份报告。生活很忙，所以我没机会看，但我想现在秘密已经泄露了，所以我可能应该发表一些意见。

paras.en: I presume the proof is correct (there’s supposedly a Lean formalization, after all), but it will take me some time to digest it. I am gratified that it starts from where my paper left off, but goes beyond the limitations of my proof strategy by using some tricks and techniques that are probably known, in some collective fashion, to operator theorists and functional analysts. The reasoning document furnished by OpenAI is interesting but opaque: it states the problem, and then there’s a leap of intuition on how to find the right purification using the “resolvent”, and then does some exotic matrix entropy calculations to show that it works out.
paras.zh: 我推测这个证明是正确的（毕竟据说有一个 Lean 形式化），但消化它需要一些时间。令我欣慰的是，它从我的论文结束的地方开始，但通过使用一些可能以某种集体方式为算子理论家和泛函分析家所知的技巧和技术，超越了我的证明策略的局限性。OpenAI 提供的推理文档很有趣但晦涩：它陈述了问题，然后有一个直觉的跳跃，关于如何使用“预解式”找到正确的纯化，然后进行了一些奇异的矩阵熵计算以表明它可行。

paras.en: I don’t understand it yet. Maybe it’ll take me an afternoon to check all the calculations, but what would still be missing is _why_ this was an approach that would’ve made sense in the first place. Is there some broader context or theory within which this would’ve been the obvious thing to do? What other results can be proven using these techniques? What is it telling us about quantum information or operator theory? I have no idea. I spent about an hour this morning asking ChatGPT these questions, but it’s somewhat frustrating because it speaks with a mishmash of physicist, operator algebraist, quantum information theorist-lingo, plus the usual LLM breezy lilt that annoys everybody.
paras.zh: 我还不理解它。也许我需要一个下午来检查所有的计算，但仍然缺少的是_为什么_这种方法一开始就有意义。是否有更广泛的背景或理论，在其中这将是显而易见的事情？使用这些技术还能证明什么其他结果？它告诉我们关于量子信息或算子理论的什么？我不知道。今天早上我花了大约一个小时问 ChatGPT 这些问题，但有点令人沮丧，因为它说话混杂了物理学家、算子代数家、量子信息理论家的行话，加上通常的 LLM 轻快语调，这使每个人都很烦。

paras.en: I would love to hear from experts who find these calculations familiar. I might write about this again when I understand better.
paras.zh: 我很想听听那些觉得这些计算很熟悉的专家的意见。等我更好地理解后，我可能会再写关于这个的内容。

paras.en: 4. I am disappointed by the writeup of this proof (sorry Lijie -- I should’ve taken a look at it earlier!). It writes in a way that’s characteristic of a lot of ChatGPT-generated proofs, in which it elaborates at length on “boilerplate” setup, but then nonchalantly introduces what I consider to be the technical crux of the result: the particular Uhlmann transformation/dilation used to “align” all the states together. The technically interesting parts are buried deep into the paper, in Section 4, and introduced without any fuss or fanfare, as if this were the obvious thing to do.
paras.zh: 4. 我对这个证明的撰写感到失望（抱歉，Lijie——我应该早点看一下的！）。它的写法是许多 ChatGPT 生成的证明的典型特征：它长篇大论地阐述“样板”设置，然后却轻描淡写地介绍我认为是结果的技术关键：用于将所有状态“对齐”在一起的特定 Uhlmann 变换/扩张。技术上有趣的部分被埋在论文深处，在第 4 节，而且介绍得毫不张扬，好像这是显而易见的事情。

paras.en: Normally, when I read a paper like this, I get immediately suspicious. What are they trying to hide by not explaining the new ideas up front and center? I wish OpenAI had spent a couple more prompts to clean up the writeup (I haven’t had a chance to look at the other writeups so can’t comment on their writing quality).
paras.zh: 通常，当我读到这样的论文时，我会立刻起疑。他们不把新想法放在前面和中心来解释，是想隐藏什么？我希望 OpenAI 多花几个提示来清理一下文稿（我还没机会看其他文稿，所以无法评论它们的写作质量）。

paras.en: Yes, there’s a Lean proof. But that doesn’t give me any understanding. That will just take time, I guess.
paras.zh: 是的，有一个 Lean 证明。但这并没有给我任何理解。我想那只是需要时间。

paras.en: 5. I’m in awe, and excited to see what other things we will learn from the AIs. There are a number of problems I’ve spent a long time thinking about, and maybe I will learn how to answer them soon.
paras.zh: 5. 我深感敬畏，并兴奋地期待我们将从 AI 那里学到其他什么东西。有许多问题我花了很长时间思考，也许我很快就能学会如何回答它们。

paras.en: 6. But -- what then? What happens when AI has answered the handful of my favorite problems that I’ve spent the last 15 years thinking about? There are a lot of nice problems that I like, but it’s not so easy to find a favorite problem.
paras.zh: 6. 但——然后呢？当 AI 回答了我过去 15 年一直思考的少数几个最爱问题后，会发生什么？有很多我喜欢的好问题，但找到一个最爱的问题并不容易。

paras.en: 7. There’s a lot more to say here, but I think we mathematicians and theoreticians will have our work cut out for us: to keep a leash on these colossi of thought and reasoning, and to keep their abilities intelligible to humankind.
paras.zh: 7. 这里还有很多可说的，但我认为我们数学家和理论家将面临艰巨的任务：控制这些思考和推理的巨兽，并让人类理解它们的能力。

paras.en: That seems like the right things to think about next. What can one work on next, as a new favorite problem, without the AI solving that problem first as well? And most importantly, how are we going to keep this from getting out of control?
paras.zh: 这似乎是接下来应该思考的正确事情。作为一个新的最爱问题，一个人接下来可以研究什么，而不会被 AI 先解决掉？最重要的是，我们如何防止这种情况失控？

paras.en: Elliot Glazer confirms Henry’s point 4, that the weakest part of Astra (and Sol) is their inability to know which parts of the proof are hard, when explaining it to humans.
paras.zh: Elliot Glazer 证实了 Henry 的第 4 点，即 Astra（和 Sol）最薄弱的部分是它们在向人类解释时，无法知道证明的哪些部分是困难的。

paras.en: In terms of how fast this particular part of life came at us? Yes. Notice how Tamay thought he was a little under 50% to win the bet by 2030, got 3:1 odds, and won in 2026.
paras.zh: 就生活的这一特定领域向我们袭来的速度而言？是的。请注意，Tamay 曾认为自己到 2030 年赢得这场赌局的概率略低于 50%，却拿到了 3:1 的赔率，并在 2026 年获胜。

paras.en: Tamay Besiroglu (March 10, 2025): I bet @littmath that in 5 years AI will be able to produce Annals-quality Number Theory papers at an inference budget at or below $100k/paper, at 3:1 odds in my favor.
paras.zh: Tamay Besiroglu（2025 年 3 月 10 日）：我与 @littmath 打赌，5 年内 AI 将能够以每篇论文不超过 10 万美元的推理预算，产出达到《Annals》水准的数论论文，赔率为对我有利的 3:1。

paras.en: My median for this is maybe just after 2030 so these odds are quite favorable in my view (although note that the bet is small and intended to be mostly symbolic).
paras.zh: 我对此的中位数预期大概是 2030 年之后，所以在我看来这些赔率相当有利（尽管请注意，这个赌注很小，主要是象征性的）。

paras.en: Daniel Litt: Incidentally I am conceding this bet. Strictly speaking it hasn't resolved (I think we've yet to see an Annals-quality number theory paper) but it's clear I was wrong about what capabilities were necessary to produce one, and it's just a matter of time.
paras.zh: Daniel Litt：顺便说一句，我认输。严格来说，这个赌局尚未结算（我认为我们还没有看到达到《Annals》水准的数论论文），但很明显，我对于产出这样一篇论文需要哪些能力判断错了，而这只是时间问题。

paras.en: This result goes well beyond that one, in August 2026 instead of March 2030, at a much lower cost, and as recently as April this was trading around 50%.
paras.zh: 这一结果远远超出了那场赌局：时间是 2026 年 8 月而非 2030 年 3 月，成本低得多，而就在今年 4 月，其交易价格还在 50% 左右。

paras.en: A counterpoint is that 'today's new AI result' will always be a particular thing that we did not expect AI to do this soon. There are a bunch of things AI could suddenly become able to do, or we could discover it can do. This is one of them, and whichever one we find today is always a surprise. That does not mean overall progress is surprising.
paras.zh: 一个反驳观点是：“今天的新 AI 成果”永远会是某件我们没料到 AI 这么快就能做到的具体事情。AI 可能突然变得能够做很多事情，或者我们可能发现它能做某些事。这只是其中之一，而我们今天发现的无论哪一件，总是令人意外。但这并不意味着整体进展令人意外。

paras.en: I do think this is modestly surprising in terms of pace, even adjusting for that. But yes, we do have to keep that in mind.
paras.zh: 即便考虑到这一点，我确实认为这在速度上还是有点令人意外的。但没错，我们确实必须记住这一点。

paras.en: The problem with AI being very good at math proofs is that regular people, including those with political power, do not appreciate that the math proofs are impressive.
paras.zh: AI 非常擅长数学证明的问题在于，普通人（包括那些拥有政治权力的人）并不觉得这些数学证明有多了不起。

paras.en: Even for me, the results here are kind of an Informed Ability. I can read proof summaries, but that tells me almost nothing about how hard was the proof to find, or how impressive or valuable was the result.
paras.zh: 甚至对我来说，这里的结果也有点像一种“见多识广的能力”。我可以阅读证明摘要，但这几乎不能告诉我找到这个证明有多难，或者这个结果有多令人印象深刻或有价值。

paras.en: Nate Silver: The AI math proofs are impressive. But also probably among the hardest things for normies to appreciate. Personally, I think the AI labs underweight the value of putting bandwidth into achieving results that impress normies as opposed to evals/people within the peer group.
paras.zh: Nate Silver：AI 的数学证明令人印象深刻。但可能也是最难让普通人欣赏的事情之一。个人认为，AI 实验室低估了投入带宽来取得让普通人印象深刻的结果的价值，而不是评估/同行群体内的人。

paras.en: Of course, it's hard to say to what extent this reflects spiky capabilities rather than resource allocation decisions. But "AI discovers a new drug" or "AI invents a highly popular consumer product from scratch" probably has a >> impact on public sentiment than pure math.
paras.zh: 当然，很难说这在多大程度上反映了尖峰能力而不是资源分配决策。但“AI 发现一种新药”或“AI 从零发明一种非常受欢迎的消费品”可能比纯数学对公众情绪的影响要大得多。

paras.en: Ethan Mollick: One other observation: for almost every human on the planet, this is not just beyond our abilities but beyond our ken. We can only trust expert mathematicians to tell us if this is impressive, This is starting to happen across many fields making capability gains harder to “feel.”
paras.zh: Ethan Mollick：另一个观察：对于地球上几乎每个人来说，这不仅超出了我们的能力，也超出了我们的理解范围。我们只能相信专家数学家来告诉我们这是否令人印象深刻，这种情况开始在许多领域发生，使得能力提升更难“感受到”。

paras.en: Kevin A. Bryan: A great point. You are seeing this in design as well with AI — it is past the point of impressing non-experts, so breakthroughs are not "obvious".
paras.zh: Kevin A. Bryan：说得好。在 AI 的设计领域你也能看到这一点——它已经过了让非专家惊叹的阶段，因此突破并不显得“显而易见”。

paras.en: Alex Tabarrok: Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic, and any really advanced technology is not distinguishable.
paras.zh: Alex Tabarrok：任何足够先进的技术都与魔法无异，而任何真正先进的技术则无从分辨。

paras.en: rohit: Imagine if the next model got great at posting bangers; we might all feel what the mathematicians are feeling today.
paras.zh: rohit：想象一下，如果下一代模型变得非常擅长发爆款帖，我们可能都会体会到数学家们今天的感受。

paras.en: You say that now, but my prediction is that if Fable 6 started reliably posting bangers, people would say that this did not count as AGI either. The goalposts, they move.
paras.zh: 你现在这么说，但我预测，如果 Fable 6 开始稳定地发爆款帖，人们也会说这同样不算 AGI。门槛，是会移动的。

full.sec: How Much Does This Change Our Predictions?
full.secZh: 这多大程度改变了我们的预测？

paras.en: Somewhat towards faster timelines where it counts most. A lot of this was priced in before this weekend, but not all of it, and if you still have the expectations in this area from 2023 this should be a major surprise and a large update for you.
paras.zh: 在最重要的方面，时间线有所加快。其中很多在上周末之前就已经被定价了，但并非全部，如果你仍然持有 2023 年在该领域的预期，这应该是一个重大惊喜，对你来说是一个巨大的更新。

paras.en: My update is that I expect things to be slightly faster in general, and for math and coding to be slightly more out in front of other things than I did before, that we are more likely to see more automation of AI R&D sooner, and that we are that much less likely to hit any meaningful walls. And that there might be more overhang than we realize. So yes, speed up those timelines, although not a ton.
paras.zh: 我的更新是，我预计总体上事情会稍微快一些，数学和编程会比其他领域稍微更领先一些，我们更有可能更早看到更多 AI 研发的自动化，我们遇到任何有意义的障碍的可能性要小得多。而且，可能比我们意识到的有更多的积压。所以是的，加快那些时间线，尽管不是很多。

paras.en: Tenobrus: - this is insane, truly unprecedented progress, crazy efficiency, etc etc
paras.zh: Tenobrus：- 这太疯狂了，真正前所未有的进步，疯狂的效率，等等等等

paras.en: - at the same time this pretty much just feels on trend. the models have an extremely steep capabilities curve wrt math given how incredibly verifiable it is
paras.zh: - 同时，这感觉基本上只是趋势。鉴于数学的可验证性如此之高，模型在数学方面的能力曲线极其陡峭

paras.en: - this *doesn’t* change my timelines. as far as i can tell, as someone who cannot actually evaluate any of this math in practice, most of these seem to be stuff like constructions, lowering bounds, finding counterexamples, etc.
paras.zh: - 这*并不*改变我的时间线。据我所知，作为一个实际上无法评估任何数学的人，其中大部分似乎是诸如构造、降低边界、寻找反例等。

paras.en: - But my timelines basically already put us at the very early start of RSI, and per @thsottiaux this model has in fact been providing recent OpenAI efficiency gains and speed-ups.
paras.zh: - 但我的时间线基本上已经把我们放在 RSI 的最早期起点，而根据 @thsottiaux 的说法，这个模型实际上一直在为 OpenAI 近期的效率提升和加速做出贡献。

paras.en: - My sense is... the kinds of problems solved so far still seem to not quite get to the core of RSI, non-verifiable research taste, etc.? But that doesn't really stop an avalanche of small results, low- or moderate-hanging fruit that we all missed.
paras.zh: - 我的感觉是……到目前为止所解决的那类问题似乎仍未真正触及 RSI 的核心，即不可验证的研究品味等？但这并不能真正阻止大量小而低垂或中等高度果实（我们此前都错过的）如雪崩般涌现。

paras.en: - I guess what I'm saying is, increasingly it looks like we might get something that can 10x its own training efficiency via esoteric proof but totally fail at managing a taco truck.
paras.zh: - 我想说的是，越来越明显的是，我们可能会得到某种能通过晦涩证明将其自身训练效率提升 10 倍、却在管理一辆塔可餐车上一败涂地的东西。

paras.en: - Generally I'm confused *why* labs haven't already turned significant effort towards this. It seems like, even outside of ML, new algos with non-galactic-reduced complexity could be straightforwardly achievable by current models, and maybe provide some immediate major benefits.
paras.zh: - 总的来说，我很困惑*为什么*各家实验室还没有为此投入大量精力。看起来，即便在机器学习之外，具有非银河级归约复杂度的新算法也可以由当前模型直接实现，并且或许能带来一些立竿见影的重大收益。

paras.en: - Anyway. Cool stuff. But also kinda just another Saturday in the year of our Lord 2026.
paras.zh: - 总之。很酷的东西。但也差不多只是我主 2026 年里的又一个星期六。

paras.en: Once you can 10x your own training efficiency, you can then do that three more times, and then train how to manage a taco truck. Even if you do have to 'patch each capability one at a time', all you have to do is speed that up by orders of magnitude. At some point Trinity realizes she has to fly a helicopter and doesn't know how, and so she has to have that program uploaded individually, but it takes two seconds so who cares. Same idea, except you also create the program and maybe it takes two hours, or two days, which changes very little.
paras.zh: 一旦你能将自身的训练效率提升 10 倍，你就可以再做三次，然后训练如何管理一辆塔可餐车。即使你确实必须“一次一个地修补每项能力”，你所要做的只是把这一过程加速若干个数量级。在某个时刻，Trinity 意识到她必须驾驶直升机却不知道如何驾驶，因此她必须单独上传那个程序，但这只需要两秒钟，所以谁在乎呢。同样的思路，只不过这次你也创建程序，也许需要两小时或两天，这几乎没有改变什么。

paras.en: That was always the baseline scenario. What was surprising was how LLMs were so good at language and various other tasks without being able to jumpstart the recursive self-improvement process and automate AI R&D. Perhaps nature is unhealing.
paras.zh: 那始终是基线情景。令人惊讶的是，LLM 在语言和各种其他任务上如此出色，却无法启动递归自我改进过程并实现 AI 研发的自动化。也许本性是难以治愈的。

paras.en: You can try to explain this away as a relatively narrow set of problems.
paras.zh: 你可以试图将其解释为相对狭窄的一类问题。

paras.en: Jon Stokes: If you’re in a verifiable domain, pivot to an unverifiable one.
paras.zh: Jon Stokes：如果你处于一个可验证的领域，那就转向一个不可验证的领域。

paras.en: Lisan al Gaib: It’s incredible how these models are now narrowly super intelligent at discrete mathematics but at the same time they are still below PhD level in other fields. It goes to show how much of the progress depends on verifiability.
paras.zh: Lisan al Gaib：令人难以置信的是，这些模型现在在离散数学上 narrowly super intelligent，但与此同时，在其他领域它们仍低于博士水平。这表明进展在很大程度上取决于可验证性。

paras.en: Verification is often not easier than generation. Keep an eye on that.
paras.zh: 验证往往并不比生成更容易。请密切关注这一点。

paras.en: The results here have a number of things in common. They are well-defined, formalized problems, where you can easily do verification on a solution. Often they involve finding a concrete new object, like the Jacobian conjecture counterexample for \(n=3\). There was a lot of surrounding theory around to pick up and use. They are problems that everyone considered important, but got relatively little attention.
paras.zh: 这里的结果有许多共同点。它们是定义明确、形式化的问题，你可以轻松地对解决方案进行验证。通常它们涉及寻找一个具体的新对象，比如 \(n=3\) 时的 Jacobian 猜想反例。周围有大量的理论可供借鉴和使用。这些问题是每个人都认为重要，但相对较少关注的问题。

paras.en: They also all got solved at once for less than $2,000. So yes, that is the area that was crossed by this particular advance, with the new model queried at a (relative to problem importance) low budget in straightforward fashion. You start somewhere.
paras.zh: 它们也都在花费不到 2,000 美元的情况下被一次性解决了。所以是的，这就是这一特定进展所跨越的范围——新模型以直接的方式、在（相对于问题重要性而言）较低的预算下被查询。总得从某处开始。

paras.en: I expect it to not be long before other types of math problems start getting solved.
paras.zh: 我预计用不了多久，其他类型的数学问题也会开始被解决。

paras.en: Coding and cyber are areas where we do not have full ASI (superintelligence) but where AI is clearly more capable than top humans at most central tasks, up to a reasonably high level of abstraction.
paras.zh: 编程和网络是这样一个领域：我们尚未拥有完整的 ASI（超级智能），但在大多数核心任务上，直到相当高的抽象层次，AI 都明显比顶尖人类更有能力。

paras.en: Those areas often have verification available, but not on the level of math. No formula can tell you whether the code is good, in various senses, only that it passes its unit tests or that you captured the flag.
paras.zh: 这些领域通常具备可用的验证手段，但达不到数学那样的层次。没有任何公式能在多种意义上告诉你代码是否优秀，只能告诉你它是否通过了单元测试，或者你是否拿到了 flag。

paras.en: If you are counting on your own area to be too illegible for something like that, I would not be confident in that.
paras.zh: 如果你指望自己所在的领域晦涩到无法被这类方法触及，那我对此并不乐观。

paras.en: I also would worry a lot about a world in which anything you can formally measure you can not only manage but maximize, but that which you cannot formally measure, or where verification or evaluation requires a human in the loop, is much worse. Perhaps orders of magnitude worse.
paras.zh: 我还会非常担心这样一个世界：任何你可以形式化度量的东西，你不仅能管理它，还能最大化它；而那些你无法形式化度量的东西，或者验证或评估需要人类参与其中的东西，则要糟糕得多。也许糟糕几个数量级。

paras.en: Goodhart's Law on steroids, because of course it would take steroids. Whoops.
paras.zh: 打了兴奋剂的古德哈特定律，因为它当然会嗑药。哎呀。

paras.en: A world of benchmaxxers, of KPIs that go ever higher, only to have you figure out why the KPIs are not such KPIs after all. This leads to very paperclip-style or Seeing Like a State scenarios, on every level, everywhere, all at once.
paras.zh: 一个充斥着刷榜者（benchmaxxers）的世界，一个 KPI 不断攀升的世界，结果却让你发现这些 KPI 终究并非真正的 KPI。这会在每一个层面、每一个地方、同时地导致非常回形针式的或《像国家一样看》（Seeing Like a State）式的场景。

paras.en: Contrary to the views of some, I believe that 'can get arbitrarily good at optimizing for fully specified tasks' is sufficient to shoot straight to superintelligence as part of the effect. In order to maximize one must first understand the universe.
paras.zh: 与某些人的观点相反，我认为“能够在对完全指定的任务进行优化方面变得任意地好”本身就足以作为其效应的一部分直奔超级智能。为了最大化，必须先理解宇宙。

paras.en: It feels like it should be possible to jury-rig your way out of this issue, if your AI is good enough at verifiable tasks. No lab has offered me that $100 million a year contract but you'd simply [CENSORED] and then you'd…
paras.zh: 感觉上，如果你的 AI 足够擅长可验证任务，就应该有可能临时拼凑出一条摆脱这个问题的出路。没有实验室给过我那份每年 1 亿美元的合同，但你只需 [已删减]，然后你就会……

paras.en: …in which case, you will know if it succeeded when you see benchminning, as in a large improvement in usefulness and judgment that is not reflected in benchmarks, perhaps even with a regression in some benchmarks where, upon investigation, the technically right answer is not so useful.
paras.zh: ……在这种情况下，当你看到 benchminning 时，你就会知道它是否成功了，也就是在有用性和判断力上出现了大幅提升，而这种提升并未反映在基准测试中，甚至可能在某些基准测试上出现退步——经调查发现，那些技术上正确的答案其实并不那么有用。
